items.message: The second paragraph runs two distinct ideas together with a semicolon: 'Only applies where `scala.language.reflectiveCalls` is imported, so that code written against Scala 2 keeps compiling; import `scala.reflect.Selectable.reflectiveSelectable` instead.' The clause after the semicolon reads as an afterthought rather than a grammatically parallel continuation. Splitting into two sentences would read more cleanly, e.g. '... keeps compiling. Prefer importing `scala.reflect.Selectable.reflectiveSelectable` instead.'

`scala.reflect.Selectable` is referenced as a wiki-style link `[[scala.reflect.Selectable]]` in the first sentence but as a plain backtick code reference `` `scala.reflect.Selectable` `` in the `@return` tag. Minor inconsistency within the same comment; picking one style throughout would be cleaner (though both are individually acceptable Scaladoc conventions).
